clue.text: War banished from English town or one in Scotland

indicators.note: banished from says the word War is driven out of the town that follows

parts.note: Warwick is the county town of Warwickshire in England

explanation.surface: A town in England was spared war, or so it seems, along with one north of the border.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing WAR from WARWICK leaves the name of a town in Caithness.
explanation.definitionFit: Wick is a small harbour town in the far north-east of the Scottish mainland.

clue.text: Turn up and bowl first in the game

indicators.note: first places the bowl ahead of the turning up in the build

parts.note: in the game of bowls each ball is called a wood
to cock a hat brim or an ear is to turn it up

explanation.surface: Instructions for a sportsman: arrive and bowl first in the match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'game' here means wild birds hunted for food, not a sporting match.
explanation.definitionFit: The woodcock is a wading bird shot as game in season.

clue.text: Master preparing courses shows such skill

definitions.text: Master preparing courses shows such skill

parts.words: Master preparing courses shows such skill
parts.note: courses here are the dishes of a meal, so the master is a chef and the skill is of the kitchen

explanation.surface: A master organising training courses shows a particular talent.
explanation.definitionFit: Cooking skill is described with the adjective for the kitchen and its arts.

clue.text: Show compassion, and be able to follow suit, perhaps

definitions.meaning: to be merciful or kind to someone

definitions.text: be able to follow suit, perhaps
definitions.meaning: in card games, holding a card of the suit led, such as one of the red suit with that shape, lets you follow suit

explanation.surface: Advice to be kind, and to fit in with everyone else.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means relent or be kind; literally it means holding one card of the suit led.

clue.text: Having more points each

definitions.meaning: in front in a contest, leading on the score
per person, as in five pounds a person

explanation.surface: A scoring note about being in the lead, per player.
explanation.definitionFit: Leading means in front on points; one per person is spoken of as so much per head.

clue.text: It's all there is

parts.note: read as a statement about everything that is, the whole of being

explanation.surface: A shrug: that's the lot.
explanation.definitionFit: Being itself, the sum of all that is, is the philosophical sense of the word.

clue.text: Does one have a slim chance' of holding up a casino?

definitions.text: Does one have a slim chance' of holding up a casino?

parts.words: Does one have a slim chance' of holding up a casino?
parts.note: holding up suggests a robbery, but means staying upright; a casino is a place full of playing cards, and a flimsy pile of them rarely stands

explanation.surface: Would a robber have much hope of raiding a gambling hall?
explanation.definitionFit: A structure of propped playing cards is the stock image of something fragile that may collapse at any moment.

clue.text: Make suggestion I'd save to be reviewed

indicators.note: reviewed suggests the letters are looked at again and set out in a fresh order

explanation.surface: Someone offers a recommendation they have kept back for reconsideration.
explanation.definitionFit: To counsel someone is to offer them a recommendation.

clue.text: Turned this creature the other way up

definitions.text: Turned this creature the other way up

parts.words: Turned this creature the other way up
parts.note: a boat that capsizes is said to turn the creature in question, lying on its back like a shelled reptile

explanation.surface: Someone flipped an animal over.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for capsizing names this shelled reptile, helpless when on its back.

clue.text: Look at some bimbo gleefully?

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Is that a leer at a cheerful airhead?
explanation.definitionFit: To leer is to look at someone with obvious desire.

clue.text: House appears to shake, note

parts.note: a semi is a semi-detached house, sharing one wall with its neighbour
to quaver is to tremble or shake

explanation.surface: A building seems to tremble, someone observes.
explanation.walkthrough: A semi-detached house is the typical British suburban home.
explanation.definitionFit: A musical note worth a sixteenth of a semibreve, the sixteenth note in American usage.

clue.text: Disastrous sequence of events, after a knock-on?

definitions.meaning: a chain reaction of failures, each triggering the next
what follows when one tile in a row is knocked onto the next

explanation.surface: A rugby fumble sets off a run of misfortunes.
explanation.walkthrough: A knock-on is a rugby foul, but here it is one tile toppling the next in a line.
explanation.definitionFit: The image of a line of falling tiles stands for any chain of linked collapses.

clue.text: Agreement whereby pet's restricted on rope

indicators.note: restricted means the pet confines the following words within itself

parts.note: a cat is a common pet
a cord is a thin rope

explanation.surface: A treaty whereby an animal must be kept on a leash.
explanation.definitionFit: A concordat is a formal treaty, especially one between a state and the Vatican.

clue.text: Facility left for support of artistic effort

parts.note: facility means ease or effortlessness

explanation.surface: A grant facility set aside to back the arts.
explanation.definitionFit: The painter's stand holds the canvas while the work is done.

clue.text: One produces shares for consumers in joint operation

definitions.text: One produces shares for consumers in joint operation

parts.words: One produces shares for consumers in joint operation
parts.note: the shares are slices for diners, and the joint is a roast of meat being cut up

explanation.surface: A company issuing stock to customers in a joint venture.
explanation.definitionFit: The long blade used to slice a roast at table.

clue.text: Start to risk cash with small northern negotiator

parts.note: go means start, as in ready, steady, go
to bet is to stake money
wee is Scottish for small

explanation.surface: A broker opens by gambling with a little Scotsman's money.
explanation.definitionFit: An intermediary who carries messages between two parties.

clue.text: British governor general

definitions.meaning: the Roman governor of the province of Britain in the first century
a Roman military commander who campaigned in Scotland

explanation.surface: A colonial official who was also an army chief.
explanation.walkthrough: Gnaeus Julius Agricola governed Roman Britain; his son-in-law Tacitus wrote his life.
explanation.definitionFit: The historical figure ruled Roman Britain and led its legions north.

clue.text: Suddenly stop riding? Time to get your skates on!

definitions.text: Time to get your skates on!

parts.note: to freeze is to stop dead
up means on horseback, as a jockey is up

explanation.surface: A rider halts abruptly, and someone urges hurry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get your skates on' means hurry up, but here it is literal: the ice is thick enough to skate.
explanation.definitionFit: A spell of hard frost when lakes and rivers ice over, fit for skating.

clue.text: It indicates a reference showing how to make a pair of stilettos?

definitions.meaning: a printer's mark pointing the reader to a footnote

explanation.surface: A footnote mark that, taken literally, is a brace of thin blades.
explanation.definitionFit: The printer's double-barred cross marks the third footnote; literally it names two blades.

clue.text: Hunting call making the majority of you sick, possibly

indicators.note: the majority of a word is all but its last letter, so its final letter is dropped
possibly signals that the letters of sick may be arranged differently

explanation.surface: A huntsman's cry that turns most people's stomachs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'majority of' drops U from YOU, giving YO; 'possibly' rearranges SICK to ICKS.
explanation.definitionFit: A traditional fox-hunting cry urging the hounds on.

clue.text: Do I find a good deal useful as a club member?

definitions.text: Do I find a good deal useful as a club member?

parts.words: Do I find a good deal useful as a club member?
parts.note: deal is pine timber, prized by a woodworker; also anyone who signs up to a club

explanation.surface: A bargain-hunter wonders whether club membership pays off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deal' is softwood timber such as pine, not a bargain.
explanation.definitionFit: A carpenter making fittings works in deal, and someone who signs up is literally one who enrols.

clue.text: Controlling current cricket sides

parts.note: the leg side of a cricket field is also called the on side
the side of a cricket field facing the batter's bat is the off side

explanation.surface: Electric power linked to the two halves of a cricket pitch.
explanation.walkthrough: A cricket field is split lengthwise into the on (or leg) side and the off side.
explanation.definitionFit: A switch of this kind turns electric flow to a device open or shut.

clue.text: Assess performance of stroke on the' river

indicators.note: on places the stroke after the river in the build

parts.note: the Test is a chalk-stream river in Hampshire, famed for trout
a drive is an attacking stroke in cricket or golf

explanation.surface: An oarsman's stroke on the water being judged.
explanation.definitionFit: To try out a car on the road before buying, and so to try anything out.

clue.text: Sort out the problem of crack

definitions.meaning: to find the answer to a puzzle
to crack a code or puzzle is to work it out

explanation.surface: A request to deal with the issue of a fissure.
explanation.definitionFit: Working out a puzzle and cracking it are the same act.

clue.text: Charming company who had to leave early

definitions.text: Charming company who had to leave early

parts.words: Charming company who had to leave early
parts.note: Prince Charming's partner at the ball, who fled before midnight struck

explanation.surface: A delightful guest who had to depart before the end.
explanation.definitionFit: The fairy-tale heroine danced with Prince Charming and ran off at midnight.

clue.text: Told to deliver trunk

indicators.note: told says the word for delivering is heard, not seen

parts.note: in cricket, to bowl is to deliver the ball

explanation.surface: Instructed to hand over a large case.
explanation.definitionFit: The bole is the main stem of a tree.

clue.text: I examine two cardinal points in new order for recruits

indicators.note: new order says the following letters are rearranged

parts.note: N and E are north and east, two points of the compass

explanation.surface: A drill instructor reviewing a fresh intake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in new order' rearranges NE plus RECRUITS.
explanation.definitionFit: An official who inspects votes or entries, as at an election count or a motor rally.

clue.text: Modern copper on beat's seen the light

indicators.note: on places the copper after the beat in the build

parts.note: to lam is to thrash or beat
p is a new penny, a copper coin since decimalisation

explanation.surface: A young policeman on patrol has had a revelation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' is a police officer in the surface, but a bronze coin here; P for penny dates from 1971 decimal coinage.
explanation.definitionFit: A lamp is a device that gives light.
